newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine, Poland say let's not isolate Belarus.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine, Poland say let's not isolate Belarus.

text.p: The presidents of Ukraine and Poland on Wednesday said they opposed the idea of isolating their neighbour Belarus, which has been criticised in the West over its civil rights record.
"Belarus is our neighbour. From all points of view we must cooperate with the Belarussian leadership as well as with the people of Belarus," Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma said.
"We have no right to reject and isolate Belarus," he told a jont news conference with visiting Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski.
"We favour long-term cooperation with Belarus and agree Belarus must not be isolated in terms of political and economic contacts," Kwasniewski echoed.
The two men were speaking two days before Russia and Belarus were due to sign a union charter.

Belarus, ruled by President Alexander Lukashenko since 1994, has been criticised particulary by the United States, but also by European bodies and international human rights watchdogs for its crackdowns on political opposition and independent media.
The 42-year-old leader has paid no bilateral visits to the West since he expanded his powers after a referendum in November dismissed as illegitimate by the West.
Lukashenko is due to sign a union charter with President Boris Yeltsin on Friday but it is unclear what shape the union will take and Minsk has ruled out joining the Russian Federation.
Kuchma, who last week signed a border pact with Lukashenko, said the leaders of Ukraine, Poland and Belarus were planning to hold a summit but gave no date.
Belarus's neighbours Ukraine, Poland and Lithuania would prefer Minsk to stay independent from Moscow and have tried to maintain friendly relations with Lukashenko.
